Subject: Re: Finlytics — next steps for customer-led load test (SLOs & allowlist)

Thanks for the call this morning, Soojin. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying Qs before we schedule the test window: 

- Goals: validate that the Redwood endpoint can sustain our peak burst of ~160 concurrent streaming sessions and keep p95 latency under 250ms for single-shot text-gen requests. We also want to confirm stable streaming behavior (chunk latency) for 1–2k tokens/session.
- Primary test: customer-driven k6 load that ramps to 160 concurrency over 10 minutes, holds for 30m, then ramps down. We may run a second pass with shorter bursts (15m) to validate autoscale behavior.

Clarifying Qs: 
1) Can you share the exact endpoint (host/port) and any headers we must include (API key vs. mTLS)?
2) Will you provide a dedicated test account or should we use a shared sandbox key?
3) Any IP allowlist steps we need to complete before Friday? Our infra team can open a window but wants an explicit list of CIDRs.

Attaching our proposed k6 scenario (rough). If we need to tweak payload sizes for streaming or test different model variants, let us know.

—Alex
Alex Jenkins
Head of Platform Engineering, Finlytics

Subject: Re: Finlytics — next steps for customer-led load test (SLOs & allowlist)

Thanks Alex — great summary and thanks for the k6 script. Short answers and proposed next steps: 

- Endpoint & auth: we'll provide a dedicated test API key scoped to your workload. For the streaming tests we attach a streaming-specific endpoint (wss://stream-us.redwood.com/finlytics/fw-4917). We'll send the key via the portal and send a separate encrypted email for the raw key.
- Test account: dedicated test account (scoped to your org) — will be pre-provisioned with rate limits configured to mimic production.
- IP allowlist: see attached ip-allowlist-instructions.txt. We need the public egress CIDRs from your k6 runner fleet (single-IP or small range preferred). If you can't provide CIDRs, we can offer a short-lived proxy agent.

SLO confirmation: to be explicit for the run we recommend validating P95 <= 250ms (single-shot), P99 <= 700ms; streaming chunk latency P95 <= 120ms per chunk and end-to-end 95th token latency within 600ms for 1–2k token sessions. If those look right to you we will add these targets to the runbook and attach pass/fail thresholds.

Proposed schedule:
- Thursday 2027-03-25 09:00–10:00 PT — preflight (connectivity, auth, small pilot)
- Friday 2027-03-26 02:00–05:00 PT — full customer-led run (off-peak from your traffic graph)

Action items:
- Alex: confirm CIDRs or accept proxy option by EOD Tuesday 2027-03-22.
- Finlytics infra: provide any custom payloads you'd like to test (e.g., 512-token vs. 2k-token).
- Redwood: we'll push the k6-compatible endpoint and test key, and upload the Redwood-side k6 wrapper to the Drive link.

I'll follow up with the test key and a short runbook. If anyone needs a different schedule, flag now.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Also confirming we want to test two variants: a lower-cost quantized model you provide and a higher-accuracy fp16 model. We expect the quantized variant to be our baseline for production.

Thanks — Priya

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>, Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@finlytics.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finlytics — next steps for customer-led load test (SLOs & allowlist)

Good questions — Vanessa here (product infra). Quick answers: 

1) Model variants: we'll expose two model endpoints for the run: /model/quantized-v2 and /model/fp16-v1. Both will be wired to the same autoscale group so you can compare throughput/latency. We'll tag results in the runbook.
2) Streaming assertions: we have a k6-ws helper in Drive that includes a small JS shim to validate chunk sequence numbers and continuity for WebSocket streams. We'll link it in the Drive file you were provided. If you prefer, our infra can run the streaming pass and produce a raw chunk-level trace (timestamped) for your team to validate.
3) IP allowlist: once you share CIDRs we'll add them to the temporary allowlist and open the 3-hour test window as requested.

Operational note: to limit blast radius we'll enforce a per-key request limit of 250 RPS during the full-run window and make a second pass at 500 RPS only if the first run is stable. That maps to ~160 concurrent streaming sessions for your expected message rates.

I'll prepare the runbook and upload the k6 wrapper + WS shim. Diego, can you confirm we have the proxy agent ready as fallback?

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Product Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Priya — we have the proxy agent available if needed (short-lived EC2 with static egress). If you can provide CIDRs by EOD we will prefer direct allowlist (simpler). Confirmed plan from infra:

- We'll provision two test keys (quantized + fp16) and attach separate metrics streams in the console so you can compare side-by-side.
- We'll enable chunk-level logging for the streaming endpoint for the 3-hour window; logs will be retained for 7 days.
- If you want us to run the streaming pass instead of k6, we can — but that changes the 'customer-led' ask. Suggest: Customer runs k6 for both control and streaming (we'll ship the shim), Redwood runs an observer pass to collect server-side traces concurrently.

Deliverables we'll upload by EOD Wednesday 2027-03-23:
- Finalized k6 scripts (with WS shim) — Drive link
- Test keys & endpoints — portal email + encrypted copy
- Allowlist confirmation (CIDRs inserted) or proxy agent details
- Runbook with pass/fail thresholds and collection points (token-level, chunk-level)

Diego Fernandez
Infra Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
